questions.title: Explain how a stationary wave forms on a string
questions.prompt: A vibration generator sends waves along the stretched string towards its fixed end. Explain how a stationary wave can form. Complete the answer.

options.text: The reflected wave has zero frequency.
options.feedback: The reflected wave retains the frequency of the driving oscillation.

options.text: The wave reflects at the fixed end and travels back along the string.
options.feedback: The fixed end reflects the travelling wave back along the string.

options.text: The wave passes through the fixed wall without reflection.
options.feedback: A fixed boundary reflects the wave rather than allowing it to travel through as the same string wave.

options.text: The wave changes permanently into a longitudinal sound wave at the end.
options.feedback: The relevant process is reflection of the string wave.

parts.correctFeedback: The fixed end reflects the travelling wave back along the string.

options.text: Only waves travelling in the same direction can overlap.
options.feedback: Opposing waves can overlap and superpose.

options.text: The two wave frequencies must be added together.
options.feedback: Their displacements add; their frequencies are not added.

options.text: The returning wave must have a different frequency.
options.feedback: A different returning frequency would prevent a stable stationary pattern.

options.text: The incident and reflected waves of the same frequency superpose while travelling in opposite directions.
options.feedback: Opposing waves of the same frequency can form a stationary pattern.

parts.correctFeedback: Opposing waves of the same frequency can form a stationary pattern.

options.text: Fixed nodes and antinodes form along the string at a resonant frequency.
options.feedback: At resonance the stable pattern has nodes and antinodes at fixed positions.

options.text: Every point has the same maximum amplitude at all times.
options.feedback: A stationary wave has varying amplitude along the string.

options.text: The nodes travel continuously from one end to the other.
options.feedback: Nodes in a stationary pattern stay at fixed positions.

options.text: Every point becomes motionless permanently.
options.feedback: The antinodes continue oscillating even though the pattern remains stationary.

parts.correctFeedback: At resonance the stable pattern has nodes and antinodes at fixed positions.
